label: sec:benzene-computation-intro
html: Benzene closes the chapter with a genuinely new structural feature. Benzene C_6H_6 as a molecular braid arranges six carbons in a ring on twelve strands, with \pi-electrons spread across the cycle rather than localised on alternating bonds. The LP dual prefers the threading link T(2,6) over any Kekulé alternation. We read the D_6 symmetry of this threading link as the experimental fact that all six C{-}C bonds have equal length. Aromaticity here is not an extra postulate but a forced output of the LP minimum on an n-membered ring.
